text:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed a spike in OOMs on nightly perf after adjusting allocator knobs for the kernel-selection PR. failing workloads are long-seq chat + batching (seq=2048, batch=6).

mike: ugh, when did we flip what? which knobs?

anya: expanded expandable_segments=true and bumped max_split_size_mb from 16->64 to reduce split churn. expected fewer small allocs, but profiler shows increased fragmentation and more GC runs.

cheng: do you have the perf traces? kernel selection fallbacks?

anya: pasted relevant snippets:
```
[alloc] request 1.2G -> slab split -> assign seg=768MB, leftover small chunks
[kv-cache] reserve fail -> trigger GC
[cuda] kernel fuser: chose fallback kernel (no tiling) for attention(t=2048)
```

perf-bot: nightly-profile: https://perf.internal/reports/3076543209 (summary: +12% peak RSS, +18% GC count) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mike: interesting — fallback kernel likely increases working set per step (bigger temporary buffers), which defeats the larger max_split heuristic. so we get fewer but bigger allocations, and the KV cache warmup interacts badly.

anya: exactly. KV cache shows heavy fragmentation: many small evicted segments intermixed with large live segments. my hypothesis: larger max_split_size causes big initial slab allocations and then leftover tiny fragments that GC doesn't reclaim quickly because garbage_collection_threshold is still low.

cheng: what's garbage_collection_threshold set to right now?

anya: 0.1 (10%). config we used:
```
allocator:
  expandable_segments: true
  max_split_size_mb: 64
  garbage_collection_threshold: 0.10
  enable_buffer_reuse: false
```

mike: two quick experiments:
- lower max_split_size_mb to 16 or 24 to avoid huge slab tails
- raise garbage_collection_threshold to 0.20 so GC is more aggressive reclaiming fragments

mike: also try enabling enable_buffer_reuse=true for the workspace allocator; that should amortize many temporaries used by the fallback kernel.

anya: agreed. I'll run a 3-arm smoke: A) max_split=16 gc=0.10 B) max_split=24 gc=0.20 C) max_split=64 gc=0.20 + buffer_reuse=true. each run: bench_mem.py --model=gpt2-xl --seq=2048 --batch=6 --repeat=10.

perf-bot: queued job ids: 78421(A), 78422(B), 78423(C)

cheng: also capture allocator histograms and kv-cache fragmentation map (use --dump-alloc-map). want to see number of free slots under 8MB.

anya: good call. will attach logs. expected timeline: ~2h per run.

mike: if B shows best balance, we can land smaller max_split default and bump gc threshold in canary. If C wins, consider enabling buffer_reuse by default for current kernel routing.

anya: one more note: kernel-selection team: could you annotate fallback reason in traces? it's currently opaque. knowing whether tiling failed due to memory plan vs unsupported op would help. cc @kernel-team (tagged in convo).

infra-bot: reminder: changes to allocator defaults require a rollout checklist and perf regression window per release playbook.

anya: got it. i'll collect results and post a short summary with numbers and alloc maps.

mike: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
